scenes.line1: How do you stop API abuse?
scenes.say: How do you stop someone from hammering your API and crashing your services? What keeps your backend safe from overload?

scenes.label: Limits
scenes.sub: Rate limiting blocks excess requests to protect APIs.
scenes.say: Rate limiting puts a cap on how often clients can call your API. It's your first line of defense against abuse.
API gateways do more than just route traffic. They handle authentication, direct requests, and enforce rate limits all in one place.

scenes.label: Back-pressure
scenes.sub: Signals clients to slow down if overloaded.
scenes.say: When things get too busy, back-pressure tells clients to chill out and send fewer requests. This keeps your system stable.

scenes.question: Where should you enforce rate limits?
scenes.right: At the API gateway, so all requests are controlled before hitting your services.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap. Should you rate limit on every backend, or at the gateway? Always do it at the gateway to catch abuse early.
